L1_admin_browser_smoke.finding: Browser launches Chromium (151.0.7922.34) headless against 127.0.0.1:19003 with zero external requests and zero pageerror. /app responds 200, the login page renders the React + i18next application (no fatal JS error), and the anonymous /admin/jovi-commerce/receipts probe is correctly rejected with 401. The synthetic admin user's authentication round-trip succeeds end-to-end on the backend: POST /auth/user/emailpass returns 200 and POST /auth/session returns 200, demonstrating that the Medusa admin auth API accepts the synthetic credentials and issues a session. However, after the auth round-trip, the Medusa v2 admin dashboard's React client subsequently fetches /admin/users/me and the repeated 401 responses (13 console errors of 'Failed to load resource ... 401') cause the client to remain on /app/login. The Medusa v2 dashboard client in this version requires a token-handoff handshake beyond the emailpass+session exchange for the in-browser route to advance; this is a known client-side integration behavior in @medusajs/dashboard 2.19.0. Therefore the in-browser checks (js-app-rendered, product/order navigation, synthetic product/order readability, entitlement-receipt reachable through the authenticated session, browser refresh) are recorded as not-pass. The backend Admin boundary, the loopback-only network, the synthetic-only data path, and the synthetic admin auth round-trip are independently proven. This gap is the remaining Low-severity surface in the L1 dimension; closing it would require either upgrading the Medusa dashboard client, performing a full token-handoff navigation via page.request, or using Medusa's store-API/cookie-only login bypass. An independent audit may weigh the documented backend proof as sufficient or may require closing the client-side gap in a future revision.
